canal_p06_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_001.text: At first light on the eleventh day, Bao laid the gate's dry supports on level paving while Jiang checked the rated hauling frame. Luo walked the feeder stop from end to end before accepting the isolation. Han shifted his last crate clear of the drain hatch. The new rope worker arrived with her ordinary gloves and asked who would call the lift. Bao showed her the calling position. Yue unwrapped her scraper and felt unexpectedly young among people who asked the right first question.

canal_p06_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_002.text: The temporary stop used boards fitted into existing guide slots above the repair reach. Luo had measured those slots in low water, but one was packed with hard silt. The crew cleared it from the bank with an ordinary narrow hoe and checked the footing before bringing each board. Yue steadied the light guide rope rather than lifting timber outside her task. Water began rising on the upstream side. Luo watched the marked limit until the closing sequence finished, then measured the ordinary leakage beneath the last board.

canal_p06_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_003.text: The leakage stayed below the working limit but refused to vanish. Yue kept staring at it as if a perfect seal would make everyone less nervous. Luo told her the support plan allowed that measured flow and kept the workers out of its channel. The leaf was to be lifted from the dry bank after the isolated reach drained through its existing outlet. Perfection would not supply a safer footing. Yue checked the actual waterline instead of waiting for an impossible disappearance.

canal_p06_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_004.text: Han's delayed customer passed on the upstream transfer boat while they waited. Its owner called something unkind about committees and low gates. Luo answered that the landing fee remained posted. The man waved without agreeing and went on. Tian watched Yue tense at the insult and asked whether she wanted to run after him with their archive extracts. Yue laughed because she had considered doing exactly that. His cargo had another working route. The canal's gate would not improve if she won an argument from the towpath.

canal_p06_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_005.text: Bao and the rope worker walked the lifting line before attaching it. A frayed tail lay outside the loaded section but would interfere with the clear path if left loose. They retied it against its holder and checked the attachment point on the leaf's intact center brace. The estimate remained below the frame's rating. Bao would confirm the load by easing it onto the balance support before committing to the full lift. Jiang stood at the release selector with Yue and made her point out the manual fallback.

canal_p06_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_006.text: The selector accepted a small prepared command through Yue's opened arm routes. The hauling actuator had its own counted stone supply; the gate's weight would never run through her body. She checked the contact path on the unloaded selector, then rested her hands while the ordinary line was made ready. Jiang said she could use one controlled sequence after the support check and stop at its scheduled release. Yue heard a limit that made her useful rather than a challenge she could defeat by concentrating harder.

canal_p06_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_007.text: Tian stayed outside the marked line with the job list and a clean cloth for tool handles. She had asked for a preparation shift, not a hauling place. Bao gave her the expected handover tasks before the loaded work began. The newer applicant trimmed loose packing strips beside her. They discovered a shared dislike of flour dust and talked as if the gate were an ordinary job. Yue liked hearing that ease. Then the support creaked, and every conversation stopped at the first calling hand.

canal_p06_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_008.text: The initial lift showed the balance load within the apparatus rating. Bao accepted the reading and checked the leaf's tilt against his chalk mark. A snagged reed mat dragged at one corner. He ordered the leaf lowered to its safe support while the crew removed the mat from the bank with a long pole. Nobody reached beneath the suspended wood. Yue had prepared the command but not sent it. Waiting through the interrupted sequence cost her pride rather than charge, which was a surprisingly cheap way to learn.

canal_p06_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_009.text: The second ease came cleanly. Bao called for the controlled lift after the line worker confirmed her clear position. Yue formed the small quarter-unit command along the prepared arm path and delivered it within the scheduled half-unit allowance. The selector changed position; the external actuator took its fourteen counted charge units. The old leaf rose slowly onto the dry supports. Yue released the command at Jiang's call and let the opened routes settle. The hardest part was resisting the urge to keep touching a task already complete.

canal_p06_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_010.text: Jiang read the supply gauge against its ordinary reference while Bao secured the leaf. The earlier bench work and this lift had used sixteen units from the original two hundred forty, leaving two hundred twenty-four in the six purchased stones. Yue copied that result after recovering enough to write clearly. The number concerned the apparatus supply, not a secret reservoir she could draw through her own arms. She could rest now while the carpenters inspected the wood her command had helped move.

canal_p06_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_011.text: With the leaf flat, its worn sealing edge looked worse than it had from the bank. The center planks stayed sound beneath the ordinary pick test. A replaceable lower cap had softened around two old pegs, and rust at its strap concealed the damaged joint. Bao had planned new sealing material and cap timber within the ordinary purchase. He would use that stock rather than shaving another season from the old edge. Luo put her palm on the center brace, relieved that the gate did not require a new whole leaf.

canal_p06_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_012.text: The metal strap came free after the carpenter supported both sides of its fixing. Bao laid it beside the old cap and showed the crew where corrosion had reduced its section. One worker said Han's private crane supplier should replace it for free. The parts had different owners and no surviving common purchase warranty. Bao entered the actual gate component for replacement from its own repair stock. A resemblance between old iron pieces could guide an inspection, but would not conjure someone else's obligation to buy this one.

canal_p06_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_013.text: Tian wrapped the removed seal fragments for disposal so they would not return to the channel. A pale seedling had rooted in a crack near the cap, thin enough to tremble when she breathed. She wanted to save it in a pot. Luo said the seedling could leave with her if she kept its old mud out of the fitted joint. Tian took it to the dry apron and found an empty broken cup. The gate was losing a garden nobody had intended to plant.

canal_p06_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_014.text: After the lifting line was unloaded, the ordinary drain crew began below Han's platform. They placed the containment tray under the flap and kept a covered passage clear beside the stores. Bao checked the hinge replacement before giving the two workers the clearing sequence. Yue watched from the dry edge while resting her opened routes. The willow branch released with a wet scrape into the tray. Packed mud followed in a slow heavy sheet, entirely ordinary and much more convincing than the dramatic rush she had imagined.

canal_p06_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_015.text: The water behind the flap fell, then stopped falling before reaching the predicted lower mark. Bao asked the householder to check her outlet basin. It still caught a thin stream from the floor seam. The mouth obstruction had mattered, but another restriction remained in the buried length. The crew stopped at the reachable limit rather than sending a person into the pipe. The householder folded her arms. She had allowed the access and waited through the paperwork. Now she wanted to know whether this was another half-repair dressed as patience.

canal_p06_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_016.text: Luo showed her the changed level on the measuring stick and acknowledged the remaining seep. The crew had a reach hook suited to the straight accessible pipe, but needed to examine the inspection cover farther along before using it. That cover lay beneath the householder's outdoor washing bench. She agreed to have the bench moved after her stored jars were set aside. Tian helped carry the empty light shelf at the woman's direction. The answer was becoming another actual piece of work, which at least looked different from an apology at the door.

canal_p06_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_017.text: The inspection cover had not been opened since an old paving repair. Its edge was sealed with ordinary mortar, not a structural wall joint. Bao checked the pipe plan and removed the thin patch with a small chisel. A nest of roots crowded the reachable channel where a neglected side joint admitted them. The public maintenance plan had included this cover, but nobody had kept its location clear. Han's platform alteration explained the difficult mouth access. It did not explain this second obstruction, and the report now had to keep both failures visible.

canal_p06_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_018.text: The roots came out in short sections using the reach hook from the dry opening. The crew avoided levering against the old pipe wall. Water began moving under the householder's threshold, first reluctantly and then with an audible pull through the outlet. Her basin stopped filling. Bao checked the repaired hinge, replaced the cover with a removable seated lid and marked the side joint for the mason's ordinary assessment. The householder went inside to touch the damp seam herself. She came back carrying the basin, empty.

canal_p06_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_019.text: Tian offered the cloth covers for moving the heavy shelf. The woman accepted after seeing the water fall. Han came with one of his workers during their agreed stores break, and together they shifted the shelf onto dry blocks. She did not withdraw her possible damage claim or become an enthusiastic member of the new committee. She thanked the people who moved the shelf and asked for the next drain-check date. Yue felt an unreasonable desire for a warmer ending, then recognized how much the concrete answer already meant.

canal_p06_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_020.text: At noon, the workers ate by the keeper's shed with the gate resting across its supports. Han brought hot water from his store hearth without attaching it to a meeting. Luo had a pot of barley and greens; each worker added food from their own provision. Yue's arms ached from the controlled sequence despite its small size. Jiang watched her take the bowl and asked whether she needed a lighter afternoon task. She said yes before inventing a reason to prove that the first morning had cost nothing.

canal_p06_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_021.text: Bao sketched the replacement cap's joinery on a scrap board. The new timber had been seasoned for fitted repair, but its outer edge still needed checking after the old cap was removed. Tian asked whether the gate would remember its new shape. Bao told her wood remembered weather better than orders. He had left space for ordinary swelling beside the seal instead of forcing the cap into a rigid bargain with the canal. Yue copied the measured gap and wondered how often she had confused a tight fit with a dependable one.

canal_p06_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_022.text: The supplier's material sheet named timber, metal parts, sealing cord and transport inside the twenty-eight-copper purchase. The actual delivered cap stock was shorter than the invoice drawing by a small but important margin. Bao measured it twice, then asked the carrier to remain while he checked the packing note. An extra narrow piece still lay under the cart's canvas. It belonged to the same fitted assembly and restored the specified length through the planned joint. The carrier had mistaken it for packing, a mistake caught before anyone cut the main timber.

canal_p06_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_023.text: Yue saw how easily the delivery could have become a accusation against the supplier. She had already begun composing the complaint while Bao found the second piece. The carrier apologized for the confused unpacking and helped set the fitted stock on the bench. Tian labeled the actual pieces so the mistake would not travel into tomorrow's work. The gate's repair needed a sound joint, not a villain sufficient to explain every inconvenience. Yue returned her premature complaint sheet to the blank side.

canal_p06_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_024.text: The old cap held a notch that did not appear on Luo's gate drawing. Beneath the rusted strap, someone had cut it to clear a replaced stone guide. Bao traced its location against the existing guide face. Repeating the notch in new timber would weaken the fitted assembly at the very place they wanted stronger. The guide's projecting corner could be dressed by the qualified stone worker already assigned to the crew's planned finishing shift. Until that happened, the new cap would stay on the dry bench.

canal_p06_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_025.text: Luo hated losing another night with the feeder stopped. The temporary boards had their own ordinary inspection and working interval, but her customers would hear only that the gate still stood out of water. Jiang pointed to the notch and asked whether she wanted a fast cap or one that lasted beyond its first swelling. She rubbed her forehead. 'I wanted both,' she said. Bao promised neither until he saw the dressed guide. The keeper took her resentment to the notice board and posted the actual next check time.

canal_p06_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_026.text: A passenger asked whether the lock had failed because a cultivator touched it. Yue wanted to give him an explanation long enough to punish the question. Tian said the old cap and guide were being repaired, and showed the checked upstream crossing still available to walkers. The man took that path after paying its ordinary fare. Yue stayed quiet until he left. Tian asked whether her silence cost another quarter unit. Yue laughed, then said it might be the most difficult part of her training that day.

canal_p06_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_027.text: The stone worker could come early on the twelfth morning. Bao prepared a dust screen to protect the open fitting surfaces and set the old notch fragment beside the guide drawing. Luo assigned the night's feeder checks to her ordinary keeper schedule, paid from operations. The repair crew's shifts stayed distinct from those standing checks. Yue would not return to the selector until her routes recovered and another actual test required it. There was enough ordinary work on the bank to fill the afternoon without asking her body for a second performance.

canal_p06_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_028.text: Before evening, three jobs remained within the day's repair shift. Bao needed careful dry fitting of the cap pieces, Luo needed a current passage notice carried to the two landings, and Tian needed the removed materials separated so usable iron did not disappear with rotten wood. Jiang would finish the supply record while another worker checked the supports. Yue could take one job and hear a different part of the bank's response to a gate temporarily absent from the water.

canal_p06_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_029.text: The gate lay pale on the paving where generations had seen only its wet edge. Yue could help fit the sound new cap, walk the ordinary detour notices with Luo or sort the old pieces with Tian. Each task had a stopping point before supper. The day's small command was complete, and her own routes needed their recovery. For once, choosing useful work did not mean discovering another way to use cultivation before the ache had settled.

choices.text: Help Bao fit the replacement cap.
Walk the passage notices with Luo.
Sort the removed materials with Tian.

canal_p06_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_030.text: Bao gave Yue the clean outer cap piece and asked her to mark the grain direction before any trimming. Its pale surface looked almost identical at both ends. She found the supplier's small mark under a smear of pitch and put the end against the wrong guide line. Bao stopped her before she cut. The joint needed the grain held against the changing wet pressure, not merely a handsome match to the gate's old stain. Yue erased her confident chalk mark and began again.

canal_p06_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_031.text: The rope worker held the piece steady on dry trestles while Yue checked the planned gap. Bao used a blunt wooden gauge between the cap and center plank, then asked Yue to repeat the fit herself. The gauge caught at one corner. She wanted to shave the cap, but the corner held a hardened ridge of old seal material. Her sharpened scraper removed it cleanly. The replacement timber now seated without sacrificing wood to a defect in the surface that received it.

canal_p06_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_032.text: Yue liked the thin curls falling from the old seal. They had no hidden meaning and gave immediate evidence that her hand had done useful work. Bao let her finish the reachable face while he bored the new peg pattern. The sound of his auger came in patient turns. She asked whether he had wanted cultivation when he was young. He said he had wanted an auger that did not pinch his palm, and later he had wanted both. She laughed and kept the scraper flat.

canal_p06_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_033.text: Bao had once tested a trace at a traveling school. He could feel enough warmth to make the teacher hopeful, but not enough to repeat the route reliably. His family could pay for either the next examination journey or a better set of tools. He chose the tools and sometimes resented how easily people called it a happy decision. Yue had expected a story that affirmed his craft. He gave her a person who still wondered about the road he had declined.

canal_p06_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_034.text: She asked whether he would try again now. Bao pointed to the gate, then shook his head. He could pay for a small test someday without promising the school his whole future. What he wanted today was a joint that would not split when the canal rose. Yue held the gauge at his chosen point while he checked the new peg hole. She did not tell him his work was better than cultivation. It would have sounded generous only because she already possessed what he had once wanted.

canal_p06_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_035.text: One peg blank showed a shallow split after Bao shaped its end. Tian had set spare blanks beside the clean stock, and they could replace it without changing the timber order. Yue marked the rejected piece with a slash and put it into the ordinary offcut tray. Bao asked her to keep it whole until the work report was complete. Its split could show why the spare had been used. The little piece deserved neither a conspiracy nor an unrecorded disappearance into somebody's stove.

canal_p06_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_036.text: The cap's two fitted sections joined on the planned stepped face. Yue held the outer gauge while Bao checked the joint's closing line. One worker wanted to draw it tight with a loaded rope. Bao used the bench clamp instead, keeping the gate's suspended lifting line entirely unloaded. The difference mattered when the clamp slipped a finger's width. Nobody stood beneath a leaf reacting to the mistake. They reset the clamp from the dry side and finished the fit at ordinary working speed.

canal_p06_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_037.text: After the joining test, Bao rubbed the new cap with a damp cloth and checked how its outer fibers took water. The proper seal gap still allowed swelling, but the newly exposed end would need its specified coating before fitting. Yue opened the labeled pot and found a skin across the surface. The supplier had warned them to remove that skin before mixing the usable material below. She followed the note instead of throwing away the whole pot because its first appearance looked spoiled.

canal_p06_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_038.text: Luo came to examine the fitted stock before her passage round. She ran a finger along the planned wet edge and asked Bao to show the allowance for the dressed guide. Yue gave the corrected drawing rather than hiding her first wrong chalk mark. Bao said the original mistake had been caught before cutting. Luo wanted the final measured fit in the work record, with the correction preserved only if it helped explain a changed dimension. A confession did not need to occupy more space than the job.

canal_p06_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_039.text: Yue left the cap covered on its dry bench and washed the old seal from her fingers. Bao entered the split peg's replacement and the successful dry fit in the day's report. The new pieces would wait for the qualified guide dressing tomorrow. Yue had learned something about timber, something uninvited about Bao's old hopes and something about her own urge to turn another person's choice into a lesson for herself. None of it made the gate close sooner, but the joint was ready.

canal_p06_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_040.text: Luo took the lower landing notice and gave Yue the upstream copy. Both described the checked walking route, cargo transfer option and next gate test time. Yue began explaining why the old joint needed more work. Luo interrupted before they left the shed. Most travelers wanted to know where to stand and what delay to expect. The detailed repair report was available at the counter for people who needed it. Yue folded the public notice with the practical lines facing outward.

canal_p06_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_041.text: The upstream landing keeper had already heard that the lock would be closed for a whole month. He showed Yue the chalk message somebody left on his wall. She read the actual check time and corrected the notice beside it, keeping the date of this current estimate visible. If the next test failed, the bank would post another estimate rather than claiming this one had promised success. The keeper nodded and asked whether the cargo transfer crew could expect two more barges before dusk. Yue sent the actual question to Luo.

canal_p06_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_042.text: A woman carrying eggs wanted to use the walking detour but feared the jostle at its narrow stair. The landing crew could carry her basket on the ordinary cart platform if she paid its posted small fare. She chose that option after seeing the clean bed and timing. Yue wanted to lift the basket for free, then remembered she could not provide the same service to every traveler arriving after she left. The priced route already existed. Helping the woman find it made her departure easier.

canal_p06_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_043.text: At the stair, a man claimed his expensive boots entitled him to pass before the waiting porter. The keeper pointed to the order line and asked him to join it. Yue expected an argument about cultivation when he noticed her cord. Instead he asked her to agree that wet stairs were unsuitable for his boots. She said the alternate level cart route was posted below. He went down muttering about its fare. The porter waited her actual turn, smiling at a comedy neither of them had needed to stage.

canal_p06_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_044.text: The lower landing had two empty boats waiting for tomorrow's gate. Their pilots wanted an evening update even if no new result appeared. Luo agreed to leave the current stop and inspection status on the reading board after her keeper round. Yue delivered that commitment when she joined them. One pilot asked her to wake him personally if the time changed. She showed the ordinary landing receiver responsible for all waiting crews. The man knew him and accepted the arrangement after a brief complaint about people who slept too deeply.

canal_p06_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_045.text: Luo paused at a shuttered food stall whose owner had lost the morning's lock customers. The woman asked whether the maintenance reserve would repay the sales she imagined losing. No current scheme promised that. Luo offered the posted repair interval and invited actual documented loss claims for the later hearing without guaranteeing their award. Yue disliked leaving with so little. The stallholder handed Luo yesterday's marked batch record anyway. An incomplete remedy still required listening to a loss somebody could actually describe.

canal_p06_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_046.text: Farther along the path, an old repair worker called Luo by a childhood nickname. He said the keeper's mother once closed the canal for three days and survived everybody's opinions. Luo smiled until he told Yue the story as if it settled her present decision. She asked him for the actual year and failure. He remembered winter ice, not autumn swollen timber. His story could comfort her without certifying today's stop. Yue saw affection kept beside its proper limit, and liked the keeper more for managing both.

canal_p06_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_047.text: They checked the detour's upper rail on the return walk. One lashing had loosened under ordinary foot traffic. Luo notified the landing crew, which closed that short section while its appointed worker retied and checked it. Yue kept arriving walkers at the stable lower waiting space. Nobody needed to cross the gap during the repair. A child asked whether the whole canal was falling apart. Luo said parts wore out, and this one had just been found before it dropped anybody.

canal_p06_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_048.text: The landing worker finished the rail check and reopened the stair with its actual load limit unchanged. Yue removed the temporary closure strip after receiving his call. A traveler grumbled that they had delayed six people for one loose cord. Luo asked whether he preferred meeting the cord after it had let go. The man did not answer. Yue might have enjoyed winning that exchange, but the next arriving woman wanted help finding the cart platform, and there was no time to admire it.

canal_p06_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_049.text: At the shed, Yue gave the clerk the corrected month-long rumor and both landing crews' evening-update request. Luo kept the food stall's offered batch record for the later actual loss hearing. Their passage walk had not repaired the gate, but it had kept current travel choices from growing around an invented deadline. Yue washed the stair dust from her shoes. She could hear Bao working on the covered cap stock, and felt how many useful jobs happened beyond the task people called the important one.

canal_p06_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_050.text: Tian set the removed gate pieces on separate cloths beside the keeper's wall. Sound iron went into a marked salvage box; the reduced strap stayed aside for the repair record before disposal. Rotten cap fragments would be taken away with the dirty seal, not burned beneath the workers' cooking pot. Yue had expected sorting to be a quiet task. Within minutes, two people claimed the same small fitting because each remembered bringing it during a different old repair.

canal_p06_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_051.text: Tian asked them to identify the fixing's actual use before deciding its owner. One remembered a private cart hinge; the other named the gate's old strap. The worn hole pattern matched the gate part. The first man shrugged and said he must have remembered a similar piece. He asked whether he could buy the salvage if the canal no longer needed it. Luo could decide that through the ordinary scrap arrangement. Yue wrote his request without letting a confident first claim carry the piece away.

canal_p06_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_052.text: A sound length of iron rod looked useful to Bao for the new cap fastening, but its dimensions differed from the specified replacement. Tian checked the supplier's part sheet while Yue cleaned the rod's surface. Bao inspected it and kept it for an unrelated ordinary spare, never in the loaded gate joint. Its usefulness would not justify changing the designed fitting late in the day. The sorting box gained a labeled reserve piece, and the new joint kept the actual parts already purchased for it.

canal_p06_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_053.text: The rotten cap held three nails that could hurt a person carrying the waste. Yue drew them from the wood with the proper ordinary claw tool while Tian steadied it on a low bench. One nail bent rather than coming free. They set that piece in a rigid waste container instead of handing it to a child who wanted dry sticks for a fire. The child complained that adults kept calling wood useless and then refused to give it away. Tian showed him the bent nail, and he chose clean offcuts.

canal_p06_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_054.text: The seedling waited in its broken cup with a leaf already drooping. Tian had put it in loose dry packing rather than its damp old mud, and the roots needed water sooner than her evening plan. Yue fetched a little ordinary canal water for the plant, keeping it away from the prepared cap's clean face. Tian laughed at herself for saving something and then forgetting its immediate need. The small mistake made Yue feel less alone than another speech about lessons would have done.

canal_p06_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_055.text: Tian asked whether Yue had ever grown anything long enough to see it flower. Yue described a bean that climbed her mother's kiln fence, then admitted her mother had watered it after she left. Tian said that still counted as a plant, though perhaps not a personal horticultural victory. They found a better pot among Luo's unused household pieces with the keeper's permission. The seedling would live on Tian's window ledge, outside the canal's repair inventory and its expectations.

canal_p06_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_056.text: Under the last cap fragment, Yue found a narrow strip of cloth tied around an old peg. It might have been a temporary leak packing or a worker's marker. Pei came to look because somebody remembered her handling an earlier repair. She recognized the cloth pattern but not its use here. They recorded the actual material in the removed-parts note without turning it into an explanation. Tian said it was strange how a scrap could invite more certainty than a living worker willing to answer questions.

canal_p06_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_057.text: Pei told them about a winter repair when the bank had gathered to sing while people worked. Tian had once liked that memory. Today she asked whether the singing helped the workers or concealed how tired they were. Pei thought before answering. Some people enjoyed it; one man had asked everybody to stop because he could not hear the lifting call. His request changed the next repair. The older story grew more useful when it gained a person who refused the beautiful part.

canal_p06_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_058.text: Yue helped Tian wrap the disposal box with its sharp contents kept inside. The sound salvage remained in the assigned store, entered separately from Han's private metal stock. Pei returned to the counter before dusk with the offered scrap-buying request. Tian put the seedling in a safe corner outside the work passage. Their sorted materials showed a gate that had been repaired repeatedly by people whose motives could not be recovered from stains alone. Tomorrow it would need a new sound cap, whoever had enjoyed singing beside the old one.

canal_p06_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_059.text: At the end of the shift, Tian gave Bao the salvage and disposal record, including the reduced strap kept for examination. The old seedling left with her, as Luo had agreed. Yue had stayed within ordinary hand work while her opened routes settled. She felt more rested than she expected after an afternoon that never touched the release selector. Tian offered to show her the plant later if it survived the transfer. Yue accepted without promising to be present for every new leaf.

canal_p06_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_060.text: The clerk received the afternoon reports before supper. The cap's dry fit was ready for tomorrow's guide dressing; both landings had current travel notices; removed gate parts were assigned to salvage, record or disposal. One small seedling had gone to Tian. Yue knew the details best where she had worked, and the others answered their own completed tasks. The repair plan no longer depended on her hearing everything personally. That made her less central, which was beginning to feel like a kind of relief.

canal_p06_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_061.text: Luo inspected the temporary feeder stop at dusk and again with the ordinary night keeper. Its leakage and upstream mark stayed within the working limits. She recorded the checked time on the counter's board where waiting pilots could read it. A pilot came to ask if somebody truly checked it after dark. Luo pointed to the night keeper standing beside her. He gave his own name, then asked the pilot to move his lantern out of the keeper's sight line. The arrangement gained a person behind its posted duty.

canal_p06_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_062.text: Yue slept badly despite being tired. She dreamed the gate's seedling grew roots through the new cap and lifted the whole leaf into branches. In the morning, the dream felt ridiculous enough to tell Tian. Tian said she would ask the plant to avoid public engineering. Luo listened over barley tea and said it could begin by staying out of her guide slots. The ordinary joke steadied Yue before she went to examine the feeder mark. Water had not changed because she failed to dream responsibly.

canal_p06_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_063.text: On the twelfth morning, the qualified stone worker dressed the projecting guide corner within the planned profile. He protected the channel from chips and checked the guide's remaining section before removing the small protrusion. Bao compared the new cap clearance against the actual face, then accepted the fit. The worker's contracted finishing day was split between this half-shift and tomorrow's drain inspection. Clean-up belonged within his accepted hours. Tian gave him the handover sheet, and he signed the completed guide task.

canal_p06_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_064.text: The cap fitted to the sound center leaf without forcing the new joint. Bao seated the pegs and metal fastenings, then checked the sealing strip's contact against the dry guide template. One peg head stood proud enough to catch. He corrected its seating before any lifting began. Yue watched from the clear side with her scraper cleaned and returned. The gate was becoming familiar again, which made it easier to imagine it already ready. The actual final surface check kept that imagination from setting tomorrow's water.

canal_p06_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_065.text: Jiang used the hand control for the unloaded selector test. Yue's routes had recovered sufficiently for her ordinary tasks, but the gate's next movement did not require another command performance. The actuator could be run by its manual selector under the same rated supply. Bao wanted both operating methods available to the keeper, including one that worked when no apprentice slept above the flour store. Yue helped label the manual release, privately disappointed and publicly aware that his plan was better for the bank.

canal_p06_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_066.text: Before lowering, the crew cleared the leaf's movement path and confirmed the guide dressing complete. The external apparatus lowered the fitted gate under Bao's call, using eight more counted charge units. The loaded line stayed clear of all bodies. At the resting position, the keeper's hand mechanism took over and the hauling attachments were unloaded. Jiang recorded twenty-four total apparatus units used so far, leaving two hundred sixteen. Yue could admire the movement without trying to claim that it came from her recovered arms.

canal_p06_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_067.text: Luo eased the feeder stop in the planned sequence after checking downstream clearance. The gate's first closure held the ordinary operating head, with a narrow leak along the new strip. Bao expected the strip to seat under that measured pressure, but he did not declare it finished from expectation. They marked the initial flow and waited through the check interval. The household with the drain stayed beside her own outlet, ready to report whether the reopened feeder changed the water under her floor.

canal_p06_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_068.text: The new strip's leakage settled below the accepted ordinary service limit. The householder's outlet stayed clear; her basin remained empty. Bao accepted the current gate fit after the repeated closure and documented the separate pipe-joint assessment still needed. Luo signed the keeper's receiving check and reopened the lock for the posted ordinary load. She put the first movement on her own hands, without asking Yue to bless it. The small grain boat entered slowly, carrying a customer impatient enough to test their confidence honestly.

canal_p06_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_069.text: The first boatman said the repaired gate sounded different. Luo asked whether he meant an observed catch or merely the absence of its old groan. He laughed and said the old groan had told him when to pay attention. She showed him the movement marks and actual waiting position. A familiar defect could become a habit people missed. Yue watched him adjust his line at the new call and thought about how rarely improvement arrived without making somebody learn another small inconvenience.

canal_p06_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_070.text: Han's customer returned from the upstream landing after paying its transfer cost. He asked Han to discount the next private loading bill. Han refused to blame the public bank for his own delivery choice, but offered the actual reduced crane service now available. The customer took that price rather than the fanciful canal ownership once included in his hopes. The buyer's agent made no comment. His deposit notice remained pending, and a useful private wharf might still be worth more alive than broken for immediate scraps.

canal_p06_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_071.text: On the thirteenth morning, the gate completed its repeat ordinary cycle with no new catch. Luo and Bao checked the fastening marks after the wood's first wet interval. Yue copied the actual dimensions and drew the joint by hand. Tian said the sketch made the fastening look like a solemn old face. Yue added a separate simple service diagram, so humor could survive in her own margin without confusing the next keeper. The actual fastening marks had held where the report expected them.

canal_p06_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_072.text: The canal received a small run of paid traffic after reopening. Current operating receipts went to their own account. The repair allocation still owed wages for completed contracted shifts, and the clerk paid each worker against actual accepted days rather than announcing that the new tolls would somehow fund everything. Yue took her first wage portion and set aside ordinary food money. She did not buy a brighter practice cord. The week had given her an older, more useful ambition: having enough money to keep a promise that required a journey.

canal_p06_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_073.text: The stone worker assessed the drain's side joint during his remaining contracted half-shift. Its accessible mortar repair could be completed without digging beneath the house. He priced the small seal within the materials already reserved for finishing and fitted it before replacing the removable lid. The householder watched the final water test. She wanted the next seasonal check in writing and got it. Her damp-board losses remained available for the later hearing. A completed drain repair could coexist with a complaint about the years before it.

canal_p06_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_074.text: Tian planted the gate seedling in its borrowed pot and found one new firm edge on the leaf. She showed Yue after supper without claiming it would live. Yue had brought a little jar of water rather than another engineering metaphor. They sat beside the window watching a passing cargo lantern. Tian said the gate work had made the public job notice feel possible. She might apply for another preparation shift, but only after fitting her paid stitching orders around it. Yue asked to hear the actual answer when she knew.

canal_p06_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_075.text: A messenger returned from the down-fork gardens with a visit accepted for the twenty-fourth day and a request that any early channel test stop above their planted beds. The garden keeper enclosed a sketch of the moved bank, not a promise that it was accurate enough to govern water. Luo kept the test restriction visible on Bao's plan. They could conduct the first diversion trial only in its bounded upper reach. The old charter's words would need current ground before they could become a working flood route.

canal_p06_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_076.text: Han asked for the next toll-share meeting time after hearing the lock reopen. His claim still had eighty copper behind it, and the repair reserve had held twenty-four apart for a possible payment. An Ru would return on the sixteenth day to compare the receiving account and actual operating costs. The meeting could not rely on a newly smooth gate alone. Yue promised to help assemble the current toll facts on the fourteenth morning. It would be another kind of weight, carried by columns instead of a lifting line.

canal_p06_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_077.text: Jiang checked the apparatus case after its ordinary use. The six stones and remaining charge would stay with the commission store for the later bounded trial. She would return for that supervised work rather than expecting Yue to use the frame alone because she had seen it lift once. She asked whether she enjoyed coming back to places after the applause stopped. She said the best faults often appeared then. Yue thought of the gate fastening marks and the orchard appointment still awaiting an accepted date.

canal_p06_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p06_078.text: At dusk, Luo walked along the reopened lock with her measuring stick tucked beneath one arm. The water had resumed its familiar level, and the new cap no longer looked pale beneath its wet edge. She thanked Yue for the small controlled sequence, the ordinary work and the patience she had sometimes shown reluctantly. Yue accepted the thanks without listing every error. Tomorrow she would help count what the canal actually earned, and discover which of those earnings had already been promised away.
